title: Backups
summary: What the built-in backup does, what it does not do, and why you need a second copy somewhere else.
html:
The backup system writes the database and the uploaded files into zip files, so there is something to restore from when a server fails.

Running one

Settings → Backup. You can run a backup now, or let the scheduled task run them on a schedule. Scheduled is the one that matters: a backup you have to remember is a backup you will not have.

backup_post_delay pauses between stages, which keeps a large backup from being killed by a shared host's resource limits.

What it needs

The zip PHP extension. Without it backups do not run and the settings screen says so. See Requirements.

The backup folder must be writable by the web server.

What a backup contains

  • The database — every record.
  • The uploaded files. See Files.

A database-only backup restores the list of your files and none of the files. Make sure both are included.

A backup on the same server is not a backup

The failure this protects against is the server being lost: a disk failure, an account suspension, a compromise, a hosting company going under. A zip file sitting on that same server is lost with it.

Download backups somewhere else, or have your host copy them off automatically. Then restore one, once, onto a test installation — an untested backup is a hope, not a plan.

Restoring

Restoring is a manual job: a fresh installation of the same version, the database imported from the backup, the files unpacked into place, and includes/config.php pointed at the new database. Installing covers the configuration side.

Restore into a new database rather than over a live one. If something is wrong with the backup you want to find out next to a working system, not instead of one.
